summary: Compare every day with the day before it and count the strictly warmer ones (T5 — neighbour comparison). The first day has no yesterday, so the loop starts at day 2.

blocks.title: Read N and the temperatures
blocks.text: N is on its own line; all temperatures come on ONE line, so we `split()` it and turn every piece into an `int`. Without `int`, `'9' > '10'` would be compared as text and give the wrong answer.

blocks.title: Count the warmer days
blocks.text: The loop starts at `i = 1` so `temps[i - 1]` is always a real day. Starting at 0 would compare day 1 with `temps[-1]` — the LAST day. We use `>` because an equal temperature is not warmer. If N = 1 the loop simply never runs and the answer is 0.

blocks.title: Short version and output
blocks.text: The comment shows the same count with `zip(temps, temps[1:])`, which pairs each day with the next. Then print `Warmer days: 3`.

pitfalls: Starting the loop at 0 → compares with the last day.
Using `>=` — equal days are not warmer.
